\label{lemma-dominate-factorizations}
Let $A \to B$ be a quasi-finite ring map. Given two factorizations
$A \to B' \to B$ and $A \to B'' \to B$ with
$A \to B'$ and $A \to B''$ finite and $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(B')$
and $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(B'')$ open immersions, there exists
an $A$-subalgebra $B''' \subset B$ finite over $A$ such that
$\Spec(B) \to \Spec(B''')$ an open immersion and $B' \to B$ and
$B'' \to B$ factor through $B'''$.

The base change map (\ref{equation-bc-dualizing})

the composition of the base change maps for $A \to A_1$ and $A_1 \to A_2$

\label{lemma-dualizing-associated-primes}
Let $A \to B$ be a quasi-finite homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Then $\text{Ass}_B(\omega_{B/A})$ is the set of primes of $B$
lying over associated primes of $A$.
statement: For any quasi-finite homomorphism $A\to B$ of Noetherian rings, choose a factorization $A\to E\to B$ with $E$ finite as an $A$-algebra and $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ an open immersion. For a module $M$ over a Noetherian ring $R$, write $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$ for the primes that occur as annihilators of nonzero elements of $M$. Then $\operatorname{Ass}_B(\omega_{B/A})=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B:\mathfrak q\cap A\in\operatorname{Ass}_A(A)\}$. In particular, this identifies *all* associated primes of the relative dualizing module by contraction, not only a one-sided containment.

Let $A \to B$ be a flat quasi-finite map of Noetherian rings.
Let $\tau \in \omega_{B/A}$ be a trace element.

in both $\omega_{B_1/A}$ and $\omega_{B_2/A}$.
\end{enumerate}

$$
\xymatrix{
Y' \ar[d]_{f'} \ar[r] & Y \ar[d]^f \\

}

statement: For a locally finite type morphism $f:Y\to X$, let $\Omega_{Y/X}$ be its sheaf of relative Kähler differentials. \label{lemma-kahler-different-complete-intersection}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $n \geq 1$ and
$f_1, \ldots, f_n \in A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$.
Set $B = A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_n)$.

\label{lemma-locally-comes-from-universal}
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ satisfies the equivalent
conditions of Lemma \ref{lemma-syntomic-quasi-finite} then for every
$y \in Y$ there exist $n, d$ and a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[d] &
V \ar[d] \ar[l] \ar[r] &
Y_{n, d} \ar[d] \\
X & U \ar[l] \ar[r] &
X_{n, d}
}
$$
where $U \subset X$ and $V \subset Y$ are open with $y \in V$,
where $Y_{n, d} \to X_{n, d}$
is as in Example \ref{example-universal-quasi-finite-syntomic}, and
where the square on the right hand side is cartesian.

For $n,d\geq1$, let $T_{n,d}=\{E=(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\in\mathbf N^n:\sum e_i\leq d\}$ and let $A_{n,d}=\mathbf Z[a_{i,E}:1\leq i\leq n,E\in T_{n,d}]$. $$\begin{matrix}V&\longrightarrow&Y_{n,d}\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ U&\longrightarrow&X_{n,d}\end{matrix}$$
cartesian. In particular, locally around $y$, $f$ is the base change of the universal quasi-finite syntomic polynomial family $Y_{n,d}\to X_{n,d}$.

Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of schemes. If $f$ satisfies the equivalent
conditions of Lemma \ref{lemma-syntomic-finite} then for every

$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[d] &
V \ar[d] \ar[l] \ar[r] &
V_d \ar[d] \ar[r] &
Y_d \ar[d]^{\pi_d}\\
X &
U \ar[l] \ar[r] &
U_d \ar[r] &
X_d
}
$$
with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $U \subset X$ is open, $x \in U$, and $V = f^{-1}(U)$,
\item $\pi_d : Y_d \to X_d$ is as in

\item $U_d \subset X_d$ is as in Lemma \ref{lemma-universal-finite-syntomic}
and $V_d = \pi_d^{-1}(U_d) \subset Y_d$,

\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-quasi-finite-complete-intersection}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $n \geq 1$ and
$h, f_1, \ldots, f_n \in A[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$.
Set $B = A[x_1, \ldots, x_n, 1/h]/(f_1, \ldots, f_n)$.
Assume that $B$ is quasi-finite over $A$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B$ is flat over $A$ and $A \to B$ is a relative local complete
intersection,
\item the annihilator $J$ of $I = \Ker(B \otimes_A B \to B)$
is free of rank $1$ over $B$,
\item the Noether different of $B$ over $A$ is generated
by $\det(\partial f_i/\partial x_j)$ in $B$.
\end{enumerate}
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq1$, and $h,f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. Put $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n,1/h]/(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ and suppose $A\to B$ is quasi-finite. Let $\mu:B\otimes_AB\to B$ denote multiplication and $I=\ker\mu$, $J=\operatorname{Ann}_{B\otimes_AB}(I)$ (viewed as a $B$-module via $\mu$). The *Noether different* is $\mathfrak D^{\mathrm N}_{B/A}=\mu(J)\subseteq B$. Then (1) $B$ is flat over $A$ and $A\to B$ is a relative local complete intersection; (2) $J$ is a free $B$-module of rank one; and (3) $\mathfrak D^{\mathrm N}_{B/A}$ is generated by the image in $B$ of the Jacobian determinant $\det(\partial f_i/\partial x_j)$.

\label{lemma-discriminant-quasi-finite-morphism-smooth}
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $X$, $Y$ be smooth schemes
of relative dimension $n$ over $S$. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a
locally quasi-finite morphism over $S$.
Then $f$ is flat and the closed subscheme $R \subset Y$
cut out by the different of $f$ is the locally principal
closed subscheme cut out by
$$
\wedge^n(\text{d}f) \in
\Gamma(Y,
(f^*\Omega^n_{X/S})^{\otimes -1} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} \Omega^n_{Y/S})
$$
If $f$ is \'etale at the associated points of $Y$, then $R$ is an
effective Cartier divisor and
$$
f^*\Omega^n_{X/S} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} \mathcal{O}(R) =
\Omega^n_{Y/S}
$$
as invertible sheaves on $Y$.
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, and let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be smooth of the same relative dimension $n$. Let $f:Y\to X$ be an $S$-morphism which is locally quasi-finite. Write $\Omega^n_{X/S}=\bigwedge^n\Omega_{X/S}$ and similarly for $Y$. Then (1) $f$ is flat; (2) with $\omega_{Y/X}$ the relative dualizing sheaf, $\tau_{Y/X}$ its trace section, and $\mathfrak D_f=\operatorname{Ann}\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_Y\xrightarrow{\tau_{Y/X}}\omega_{Y/X})$, the closed subscheme $R=V(\mathfrak D_f)$ is locally principal and is exactly the zero scheme of the determinant of the differential $df:f^*\Omega_{X/S}\to\Omega_{Y/S}$, i.e. of $\bigwedge^n df\in\Gamma(Y,(f^*\Omega^n_{X/S})^{-1}\otimes\Omega^n_{Y/S})$. (3) If $f$ is étale at each associated point of $Y$, then $R$ is an effective Cartier divisor and the canonical line-bundle isomorphism $f^*\Omega^n_{X/S}\otimes\mathcal O_Y(R)\cong\Omega^n_{Y/S}$ sends the canonical defining section to $\bigwedge^n df$.
